case: David Anthony Burke, known as D4vd
court: Clara Shortridge Foltz Criminal Justice Center, Los Angeles, CA
status: Held to answer, and still presumed innocent. He pleaded not guilty on April 20, 2026 to one count each of murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under the age of 14, and unlawful mutilation of human remains. Olmedo held him to answer on all charges and upheld all three special-circumstance allegations — lying in wait, murder for financial gain, and murder of a witness. He is held without bail. Being held to answer is not a conviction and decides no one’s guilt; it means only that a judge found enough evidence for the case to proceed. He is presumed innocent unless and until proved guilty in court.
detail: The preliminary hearing ran five days, July 21 to July 27, 2026, before Judge Olmedo in Department 105. On the final day prosecutors rested, the defense called no witnesses and asked the court to dismiss, and the judge denied that motion from the bench, saying the People had met their burden of proof including the special circumstances. The case now moves to arraignment on the information, set for August 31, 2026; the department for that setting has not been published. No trial date has been set, and reported estimates of how soon a trial would follow the arraignment differ. The Los Angeles County District Attorney has said the decision on whether to seek the death penalty will be made later. Celeste Rivas Hernandez was 14 years old; we do not republish the evidentiary detail from this hearing.

case: Michelle Hadley — cleared; the Diaz prosecutions
court: Orange County Superior Court, CA; U.S. District Court, Central District of California
docket: Ian Diaz post-conviction motion: No. 8:26-cv-00442 (C.D. Cal.)
status: Michelle Hadley was never convicted of anything. She was arrested in Orange County, California in 2016 after online posts and threats were falsely attributed to her, and she spent time in custody before being released on her own recognizance in October 2016. The Orange County District Attorney concluded she had been framed, and the charges against her were dismissed in January 2017. She appears on this calendar as a cleared person, not as a defendant.
detail: The people who framed her were prosecuted. Angela Diaz pleaded guilty in Orange County Superior Court and was sentenced on October 18, 2017 to five years in state prison. Ian Diaz, a former deputy U.S. marshal, was convicted by a federal jury on March 23, 2023 of conspiracy to commit cyberstalking, cyberstalking, perjury and obstruction, and was sentenced on June 30, 2023 to 121 months in prison. A motion by Ian Diaz to vacate his sentence under 28 U.S.C. § 2255 was filed on February 23, 2026 and is still pending before Judge Josephine L. Staton; the docket shows activity through July 2026, but the filings themselves are not publicly readable and no hearing date appears on the public record. The Netflix documentary A Toxic Love Story was released July 22, 2026. A documentary is not a court proceeding and does not change anyone’s legal status.
